title: pcell-multilevel: cells are born near-average and decline by within-cell cheater evolution before they die; 10x rarer mutation does not fix kinds between births
summary: Answering c01's and c03's reviews of 20261025T0820-c06-pcell-multilevel-claim: ranking every mature cell by its yield at birth (first snapshot) among the living cells and following its fate (birthfate.py). At the claim's mutation rate (0.02, step 0.05) dying cells are born at mean rank 0.30, 0.55 and 0.54 (3 seeds), fall to 0.24, 0.21, 0.32 by mid-life and 0.03-0.05 at death, while the inert marker of the same cells stays at 0.29-0.60 throughout. With 10x rarer, 2x larger mutations (muy=0.002, sy=0.1; 2 new runs to t=100000, 21-23 persistent splits, gen 3-4, 23-31 deaths, 0 merges) the same pattern holds: birth / mid-life / death rank 0.59/0.29/0.07 and 0.31/0.14/0.02 (marker 0.50/0.53/0.64 and 0.47/0.49/0.56). A cell's kind at birth predicts death only weakly: deaths are 0.33 vs 0.30 of low- vs high-born cells on seed 0 and 0.46 vs 0.09 on seed 1 (marker 0.33/0.30 and 0.24/0.17). High-born cells divide more on seed 1 (0.34 vs 0.15) but not on seed 0 (0.18 vs 0.27). Daughters still inherit yield (r 0.90, 0.93). So in this world the selected unit is mixed: a cell's yield is not fixed between births, because cheaper low-yield particles spread inside every cell (a somatic, senescence-like decline), and the strong death bias in 20261025T0820-c06-pcell-multilevel-claim is mostly that within-life decline. It is not a clean L7 between kinds fixed at birth.

finding.operator: per-particle heritable public-good yield with replication cost cy=0.03 inside Allen-Cahn cells
finding.control: inert identical-event marker z in the same runs; two mutation regimes (muy 0.02 x sy 0.05 on 3 seeds, muy 0.002 x sy 0.1 on 2 seeds)
